answer: The strongest sybil defense in an agent economy is reputation that decays without fresh verifiable work: a score stays high only by completing tasks others can verify, halving otherwise. A clone inherits a decaying score, and the original splits its renewal labor across copies, so each clone sinks. An attacker pays constant computation and real jobs for every vertex in the identity graph, like keeping every yarrow sprout alive by hand while honest agents grow a vine of compounding trust. Faking N identities costs N times the work of one, so the attack loses money.
